opening: hi, my boss said I should try this with our customer file. not really sure where to start

facts.situation: I work in retention at a small internet provider. Every month some people just leave and we only notice after they're gone.
facts.goal: I want to know before the month starts which of our current customers are likely to quit, so we can call them first.
facts.data: the file I uploaded has everyone with their plan, tenure, spend, tickets, and a column if they churned the next month.
facts.decision: my team has time to call maybe a small slice of the base each month, so we need to pick who gets a call.
facts.other: we tried just calling people with many tickets but it felt random.

opening: Hello. We have a problem with our numbers in the hotel and I need some help please

facts.situation: I manage revenue for a beach hotel. Too many rooms get cancelled at last minute and we end up with empty rooms.
facts.goal: When a new booking arrives I want to see how likely it will be cancelled, so we can overbook a bit on risky dates.
facts.data: Bookings export from our system, with lead time, channel, nationality, free cancel flag and if it was cancelled in the end.
facts.decision: decide per booking if we ask for deposit or not, and how many extra rooms to sell.
facts.other: the channel managers say OTA bookings are worst but I am not sure.

opening: we keep losing slots at the clinic, can your tool do something about it?

facts.situation: I'm the practice manager at a physio clinic with three locations. Patients book and just don't show up, maybe one in eight.
facts.goal: for each appointment booked for next week i want a flag for the ones that will probably be a no-show so reception can send extra reminders or double book.
facts.data: we have about two years of appointments in our booking software, with patient age, days between booking and visit, past no-shows, weather maybe. I can export as csv later.
facts.decision: reception decides every morning who gets a phone reminder.
facts.other: patient names I would rather not upload.

opening: I need a weekly report for our dispatch team about late shipments

facts.situation: I run operations at a regional freight company. Our customers get angry when trucks arrive late and we only find out on the day.
facts.goal: the 'report' i mean is a list every monday of the shipments planned for this week that are likely to be late, before they leave, so we can reroute or warn the client.
facts.data: we have shipment history with route, carrier, pickup time, weight, weather, and the actual delivery time vs promised.
facts.decision: dispatchers choose which loads to swap to a more reliable carrier.
facts.other: not interested in charts of last month, we already know last month was bad.

opening: Our marketing is kind of one size fits all right now, looking for ideas

facts.situation: I'm marketing lead at a SaaS for small accountants. We send the same newsletter to everyone.
facts.goal: I'd like to discover natural groups of customers in our data, like 3 to 6 types, based on how they use and pay, so each gets different messaging.
facts.data: uploaded our customer table: plan, tenure, monthly spend, support tickets, city, signup date. The 'segment' column is just SMB/mid from sales, it's old and nobody trusts it.
facts.decision: we'll build a different email track and offer for each group.
facts.other: I want the groups to be explainable in plain words for the team, like 'the cheap loyal ones'.

opening: we have lots of donor data and dont really use it

facts.situation: im fundraising coordinator at an NGO for clean water. we have years of donations, events attended, how they found us.
facts.goal: we want the data to show us what kinds of donors we actualy have - find personas we dont know yet, not the categories we already made up.
facts.data: a donor CRM export, one row per donor with gift amounts, frequency, first gift date, channel, age band. can share later.
facts.decision: plan different appeals for each persona for the year end campaign.
facts.other: small team, no data person at all.

opening: can you build me a model of our customers? want to understand them better

facts.situation: I'm the new COO of a meal-kit subscription. The board asked me to present who our customers are.
facts.goal: honestly I just need the picture of today: how many per plan and city, avg spend and tenure per segment, how churn looks across the segments we already have.
facts.data: the customers file I uploaded, with segment, plan, city, spend, tenure, tickets and churn.
facts.decision: it goes into my board slides next week, nothing automated.
facts.other: when I said model I meant like a profile, not AI predictions. I don't need to forecast anything.

opening: got our order export here, wanted to look into it a bit

facts.situation: We sell kitchen tools online and in two shops. I'm the owner, doing everything myself.
facts.goal: Want to know which product categories and which channel brought most revenue last year, and how many orders got returned or cancelled by region.
facts.data: the sales file has order date, region, channel, category, amount, status and customer id.
facts.decision: decide which categories to reorder more of for next season.
facts.other: just one-off numbers, I won't look at it every week.

opening: hi i have the bookings sheet from our tour company, what can you tell me

facts.situation: we're a small tour operator doing trips to the mountains and the coast. me and my partner split the planning.
facts.goal: i want to know from what already happened: which destinations sell to which nationalities, average lead time per destination, and cancel rate with vs without free cancellation.
facts.data: uploaded the bookings, it has everything from last two seasons.
facts.decision: we'll use it to decide where to advertise abroad next year.
facts.other: no need for anything ongoing or predictive, just the facts please.

opening: The school governors want some evidence about attendance. Can you help?

facts.situation: I'm deputy head at a secondary school. Governors asked if attendance differs between year groups and between pupils on free meals and others.
facts.goal: Compare absence rates for last academic year across year groups, gender and free school meals status.
facts.data: I can export a table of pupils with year group, FSM flag, gender and sessions missed from our MIS.
facts.decision: It'll go in a paper for the next governors' meeting to decide where to put our attendance officer's time.
facts.other: Just last year's figures, a one-time thing.

opening: quick question about our warehouse picks, there's something off

facts.situation: i supervise a distribution centre for a pharmacy chain. some shifts feel slower than others.
facts.goal: want to see average picks per hour by shift, by zone and by picker experience for the past 3 months, and error rate per shift.
facts.data: the WMS gives a log of every pick with timestamp, picker id, zone, shift and if it was a mispick.
facts.decision: decide if we need to move experienced pickers to the night shift.
facts.other: i'm not asking to forecast, i want to see what happened.

opening: hey, i need to get some customers out of this file for my team

facts.situation: I'm in customer success at a phone plan company. My manager wants a call campaign this week.
facts.goal: I need a list of the actual customers on the premium plan in Lisbon and Porto with more than 3 tickets in last 90 days, with their ids and spend, so I can download it as excel.
facts.data: the customers table I uploaded.
facts.decision: the agents will call each person on the list.
facts.other: I don't need scores or charts, just the rows with the columns cleaned up.

opening: our sales data is a mess, cant do anything with it like this

facts.situation: I'm a finance analyst at a furniture wholesaler. The export from the old ERP has duplicates, regions spelled different ways, some amounts as text with currency signs.
facts.goal: I want one clean table: no duplicate orders, region names fixed, amount as a number, and dates in one format, with a column for month.
facts.data: uploaded the sales export, order id, date, region, channel, category, amount, status, customer id.
facts.decision: I'll load the clean table into our accounting system and excel models.
facts.other: the analysis I will do myself after, I just need the clean file.

opening: I have like five spreadsheets from different branches and my director wants one thing

facts.situation: I'm office manager at a chain of dental clinics. Each branch keeps its own patient visits sheet, different column names and orders.
facts.goal: combine all branches into one table with the same columns, a branch column added, and the treatment codes mapped to one list.
facts.data: five excel files, one per branch, about a year each. Some have dates as day/month and others month/day.
facts.decision: the director will do her own pivot tables from the combined file.
facts.other: I am not a technical person, please keep it simple.

opening: machine data question - we log a lot from the line but its unusable

facts.situation: process engineer at a plastics factory. Sensors write one row per reading per second, long format with sensor name and value.
facts.goal: I need it reshaped to one row per minute per machine, with a column per sensor (averaged), and joined with the batch table so each minute has its batch number.
facts.data: sensor log as csv, plus a batch table with machine, start and end time of each batch.
facts.decision: our quality team will then use that table in their own SPC software.
facts.other: no ML needed right now, first we need a usable table.

opening: the regional managers keep asking me for numbers every monday

facts.situation: I'm a sales ops guy at a building materials distributor. Every week I build the same excel by hand for the regional managers.
facts.goal: I want something they can open anytime that shows revenue by region, channel and category, updated when new orders come in, with a filter for the week.
facts.data: the sales file I attached, we get a new export daily.
facts.decision: managers check it themselves to chase their targets, I stop sending excels.
facts.other: it should stay current without me doing anything.

opening: we're opening a new food bank site and need to keep an eye on things

facts.situation: I coordinate volunteers and stock at a food bank network, now three sites.
facts.goal: a screen the coordinators can look at every day with stock levels per category, parcels given per site and volunteers hours this week, refreshing on its own.
facts.data: we have a google sheet for stock in/out and another for volunteer sign-ins, both updated daily.
facts.decision: coordinators decide when to request more donations or move stock between sites.
facts.other: the board also wants to look at it once a month.

opening: Need help with the KPIs for our support team

facts.situation: Head of support at a B2B software company, 12 agents, tickets in Zendesk.
facts.goal: I want a live view of first response time, resolution time, backlog and CSAT per agent and per product, that updates through the day.
facts.data: Zendesk export of tickets, can be pulled automatically every hour.
facts.decision: team leads use it in the daily standup to rebalance queues.
facts.other: We had a one-off analysis last year, it was out of date in a week.

opening: something happened to our sales and nobody can tell me what

facts.situation: I own a sports nutrition brand selling via our website, Amazon and some gyms.
facts.goal: revenue in september fell a lot compared to august and I want to know why: which region, channel or product dragged it down, and what we should do about it.
facts.data: the sales file I uploaded, covers this year.
facts.decision: decide if we cut the Amazon ad budget or fix something else before Q4.
facts.other: my marketing guy says it's seasonal but I don't buy it.

opening: This summer felt different at the resort. Can you look?

facts.situation: I'm general manager of a family resort. Bookings this summer were weaker than last summer even though we lowered prices.
facts.goal: Understand what changed between last summer and this one, which markets and channels dropped, was it cancellations or fewer bookings, and what to do for next season.
facts.data: I attached the bookings, both summers are in there.
facts.decision: decide our pricing and which markets to push for next summer.
facts.other: the owners want an explanation I can defend, not just charts.

opening: our cancellations went up and the CEO is asking questions

facts.situation: ops director at an online electronics retailer. The share of cancelled orders jumped this quarter vs last.
facts.goal: find what drives the rise between the two quarters, which categories, channels, regions, and give me 2-3 actions.
facts.data: uploaded sales with order status, so cancelled is in there.
facts.decision: I present causes and actions to the CEO on friday.
facts.other: we changed payment provider in july, might matter.

opening: Margins at the bakery shops arent what they used to be

facts.situation: I own four bakery shops. This year profit is down compared to last year though we look busy.
facts.goal: I want to understand why profit dropped year on year, is it flour prices, staff hours, product mix or fewer customers, and what I should change.
facts.data: I have monthly sales per shop and product, costs from the accountant, and staff rota hours, in excel.
facts.decision: decide whether to raise prices, cut a product line or reduce opening hours in one shop.
facts.other: I'm not good with numbers, plain explanation please.

opening: i keep hearing about this thing and wondered if it's for us

facts.situation: I run HR at a mid-size logistics company. A vendor is pitching us 'AI attrition prediction'.
facts.goal: I just want to understand what that really means, how such a prediction works, what data it needs, and what the risks are like bias or privacy, before the meeting.
facts.data: nothing to share right now, I don't want to upload employee data.
facts.decision: decide if we even take the vendor meeting seriously.
facts.other: please explain in normal words, no coding.

opening: our analyst left and I'm stuck with something she started

facts.situation: I'm product manager at a small bank's mobile app team. Our analyst ran an A/B test on a new onboarding screen before she left.
facts.goal: I need someone to explain what statistical significance and a p-value mean, and whether running the test for only one week is a problem, so I can read her slides.
facts.data: only her slides, no data, and I don't need anything recalculated.
facts.decision: decide whether to trust the result and roll out the new screen.
facts.other: keep it simple, I have a business background.
